title: Quality rules and a quarantine table that loses no rows
objective_text: Apply data quality checks in PySpark: name why each bad row fails, keep good rows in silver and the rest in a quarantine table.
scenario: The facilities team's temperature dashboard shows gaps, and nobody can say whether the sensors stopped or the pipeline dropped their readings. Split bronze.readings into a silver table of good readings and a quarantine table that says why each other reading was set aside, so that every reading can be accounted for.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: A Delta table bronze.readings (8 readings) in the exercise folder and a starter answer.py.
required: A row's reason is the first rule it breaks: missing_device, missing_time, missing_temperature, then temperature_out_of_range (below -50 or above 60).
silver.readings has the rows that break no rule, with the bronze columns.
silver.readings_quarantine has every other row, with the bronze columns and reason.
Every bronze row is in exactly one table, and running the code again leaves both tables the same.

expected.description: silver.readings has readings 1, 2 and 7; the quarantine has 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 with their reasons.

verifies: Your PySpark splits rows into a valid table and a quarantine with the right reason for each, NULLs included, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves both tables the same.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace, and it isn't a Lakeflow pipeline expectation: it doesn't show expectation metrics in the pipeline event log.
hints: Build one reason column with F.when(...).when(...): it is NULL when a row breaks no rule.
Reading 5 has no temperature. A filter on temperature <= 60 and one on its opposite both drop it; check isNull first.
-50 and 60 are inside the range: out of range is temperature < -50 or > 60.
valid = checked.filter(reason is NULL) without the reason column; quarantine = checked.filter(reason is not NULL). Overwrite both.
explanation: Compute one reason column with a when chain in rule order, testing NULLs explicitly, so it is NULL exactly for good rows. Split on that column: rows with no reason go to silver.readings without it, and the rest go to the quarantine with it. A pair of filters on a condition and its negation would lose every row where the condition is NULL, such as a missing temperature, because a filter keeps only rows where its condition is true. Treat -50 and 60 as in range, and overwrite both tables so a rerun doesn't duplicate them.
troubleshooting: A reading is in neither table: the split uses a condition and its negation, which both drop NULLs.
Readings of exactly -50 or 60 are quarantined: the range check excludes its edges.
silver.readings still has bad rows: it is written from the bronze rows, not the checked ones.
reset: Reset rebuilds bronze.readings from setup.sql, removes the two silver tables and puts the starter back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
